evidence.notes: R-related to EI-10717 (see its note) — the ATTRIBUTION half: apps/operator-vite owns a typecheck ratchet that counts FOREIGN errors from packages it imports but does not own, so an error introduced in operator-core reds a stranger's gate and lands on whoever next touches operator-vite. PARTIALLY SUPERSEDED, deliberately NOT discarded: the specific mechanism this item asked for — operator-core having a typecheck of its own — now EXISTS as `npm run lint:tsc` (scripts/lint-tsc.mjs:167, `tsc -p packages/operator-core/tsconfig.json --noEmit`), so operator-core errors are catchable at their own boundary. What I did NOT verify is whether lint:tsc is ENFORCED anywhere automatic (a green-checkpoint gate step, a CI job) as opposed to being a lever agents are told to run by hand. That distinction decides the whole item: an unenforced typecheck does not stop a foreign error from reaching operator-vite's ratchet, so the attribution defect would survive its own fix. Merit left UNTRIAGED for exactly that reason rather than guessed in either direction.

_claimSubjectBaseline.body:
## The symptom
The rig (Lm1ABoMR), running a bundle that CONTAINS fix C (composedAt 2026-07-27T11:44:22Z), receives the canonical key in a refusal every single tick and never adopts it:

```
[2026-07-27T11:51:22.768Z] [git-sync] papercusp: ref-announce receive fetch FAILED for
IXfGu216EI/z (event 441080); holding cursor at 440845 to re-dial next tick:
no git process ran: duplex error: pot-git serve refused: superseded-repo-key:gh-1223568103
```

Five of these in a single tick. The correct canonical key `gh-1223568103` is sitting in the error text. Nothing adopts it. The rig's `papercusp.git` still holds ZERO namespaces.

## The root cause — reachability, not logic
`adoptRefusedRepoKey` is correct and well-guarded. It has exactly ONE production call site:

- `git-sync-action.ts:2034` — inside the BOOTSTRAP leg's dial path.

But the refusal that carries the repair arrives on a DIFFERENT leg: the ref-announce RECEIVE leg (`git-sync-action.ts:~2345`, the `cursorDecision.fetchFailed` loop). That loop has `f.stderr` containing the verbatim refusal text — and does nothing with it but `console.warn`.

So the one channel on which the repair reliably and repeatedly arrives is the one channel that cannot act on it.

## Why this is the mirror image of fix D
Fix D's own comment (git-sync-action.ts:1839) says the probe must sit ABOVE the warm gate because "a probe placed after the gate would never fire on precisely the machine that needs it: the stuck one." Fix C has the same defect in a different dimension: its receiver is on the cold-join path, so it never runs on the machine whose ref-announce leg is the thing actually dialing.

## The fix
Call `adoptRefusedRepoKey` from the ref-announce receive leg's fetchFailed handler, using `f.stderr` — the same fail-soft, next-tick-effective contract the bootstrap call site already uses. Adoption is idempotent (`already-canonical` is a clean no-op on every later refused dial), so calling it from both legs is safe by construction.

## Broader lesson (worth keeping)
A REFUSAL THAT CARRIES ITS OWN REPAIR ONLY HEALS IF EVERY LEG THAT CAN RECEIVE IT KNOWS HOW TO READ IT. Wiring the receiver into one leg makes the feature look done and tested while leaving it inert on the live path.

evidence.notes: PREMISE VERIFIED AND THE DEFECT IS LARGER THAN FILED. The item reports that sibling work-items can share one payload.plan_item stamp, so completing a SUB-LANE child flips its PARENT's plan item to done via finishPlanStamp(), and states 126 plan items affected with 51 still live. Measured 2026-08-22 over harness_shared.work_items in papercusp-workspace: 4,602 stamped rows across 4,337 distinct (plan_slug,item_id) stamps, of which 200 stamps are SHARED by more than one row, spanning 465 rows, and 83 of those shared stamps still have at least one live (non-done/dropped/deprecated) sibling. So the true figures are 200 affected stamps (filed: 126) and 83 with a live sibling (filed: 51) — the filer UNDER-CLAIMED by ~1.6x on both. That is the THIRD independent confirmation of D-026 s4's direction-of-error rule, on a third unrelated finding, and it is now safe to treat "a filed number is a floor to re-measure" as established rather than suggestive. R-related to EI-20577421906951067, not a duplicate: this one is the OVER-FIRE (things get closed that should not be), that one is the IRREVERSIBILITY (a wrong closure cannot be undone). They are two halves of one trap and neither is safe to fix alone — fixing only the over-fire leaves existing bad closures stuck; fixing only the reopen path leaves the source of them running. Both are complaints against the very reconciler whose existence supersedes EI-2443/EI-2725 in this same batch.

report.message: durable admission record could not be persisted: canceling statement due to lock timeout | sqlstate=55P03 — task exits 1 and is counted as a test failure; retry re-hits the same error

_claimSubjectBaseline.body:
OBSERVED in the canonical run 7 log (/tmp/p005-run7-runlog.stripped, run=241941-199610b3).

The task `@papercusp/operator-core :: lint:prompt-projections` emitted:

  AFFECTED_TASK_OUTPUT_BEGIN task="@papercusp/operator-core :: lint:prompt-projections" label=initial lane=serial workers=15 memoryMb=15360 exitStatus=1 signal=none error="durable admission record could not be persisted: canceling statement due to lock timeout | sqlstate=55P03"

and the SAME error on its `label=retry` attempt.

WHY THIS IS A BUG, not just an unlucky run:

1. FALSE RED. The guard itself is green. Re-run at HEAD: `node scripts/check-prompt-projections.mjs` exits 0 — canonical libs/papercusp/packages/harness/blueprints/base/prompts/su.md (sha256 0b998acc8bf0d3c3d128edc021ad4c5e31860df6905ecd61c003ebf8c8df72bb, 74226 bytes) matches both generated projections, mismatches=[]. The exit 1 was produced by the admission layer, not the check.

2. INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM A GENUINE FAILURE. The task surfaces only as exitStatus=1. It landed in `unattributed` (reason=no-file-rows) purely because it emits no per-file rows — i.e. it was excluded from the file-level accounting by accident of shape, not because anything recognized it as infrastructure. A guard that DID emit file rows would have been reported as a plain red with no hint that the cause was a lock timeout.

3. THE RETRY DOES NOT RECOVER IT. Both attempts failed on the identical sqlstate=55P03. A retry that re-enters the same contended write path cannot clear a lock-timeout class, so the retry budget is spent without changing the outcome.

CONSEQUENCE. This inflates a canonical run's failure count with non-verdicts. The repo already has the correct concept — capability:bash_output distinguishes failure_class=infrastructure-resource-limit with test_verdict=undetermined, and the plan's own D-006/D-019 say an undetermined run is not a verdict — but affected-tests does not apply it here. On a full-suite run that must exit 0 to satisfy P-004, an infrastructure lock timeout is currently able to block the gate indefinitely, and every agent triaging it will go read a guard that is perfectly green.

CORRECT STATE. An admission/ledger persistence failure should mark the task `undetermined` with an explicit infrastructure failure_class — never fold it into the failed-task count as if the task's own command had failed — and the retry path should either back off against lock contention or report that it re-hit the same infrastructure class rather than consuming an attempt silently.

_claimSubjectBaseline.body:
## What I measured

`routines:list { name:'work-item-admission-promoter', installSlug:'papercusp' }` at 2026-09-02T22:31Z:

```
cron: 0 */30 * * * *   active: true   targetRole: system:work-item-admission-promoter
lastFiredAt: 2026-09-02T22:30:57.254Z
nextFireAt:  2026-09-02T23:00:00.000Z
health: { last_error: "The usage limit has been reached" }
```

The routine is **firing on schedule and failing inside the tick.** Its sibling `work-item-admission-fail-open` is healthy (`health: null`, fired 22:16:53Z, next 22:45).

Admission census, `harness_shared.work_items`, workspace `papercusp-workspace`, last 6h, `lane IS DISTINCT FROM 'observation'`:

| admission | n | oldest | newest |
|---|---|---|---|
| (null) | 949 | 16:31 | 22:30 |
| unreviewed | 76 | 16:32 | **21:10** |
| auto | 34 | 16:41 | 22:17 |
| pending | 17 | **21:28 (64 min)** | 22:22 |

The oldest `pending` row is **past the 60-minute fail-open guarantee** the claim refusal advertises, and no fail-open promotion has landed since 21:10.

## Verified at the source, not inferred from bucket names

`work-items-admission-promoter.ts:2179` — `SET admission = 'unreviewed', admitted_at = now(), admitted_by = ${FAIL_OPEN_ACTOR} ... AND admission = 'pending'`. So `unreviewed` is written by the FAIL-OPEN path specifically. That is what makes the census above readable: a growing `pending` bucket with a frozen `unreviewed` high-water mark is the promoter not screening, with the backstop not yet eligible.

## The actual defect — the silence, not the outage

A `system:*` targetRole means this routine is LLM-backed, so account starvation takes out its whole tick. A coord broadcast at ~22:32Z reads `infra-liveness RECOVERED (accounts-starved)`, which names the mechanism and says it has since cleared — so this instance is a self-recovering flap.

That does not make it a non-issue, for one reason: **the degraded mode is indistinguishable from the healthy one at every surface an agent or operator actually looks at.**

- Items still get admitted, so nothing appears broken.
- They are admitted `unreviewed` by `FAIL_OPEN_ACTOR` — i.e. **never duplicate-screened at all** — which is precisely the safety property admission exists to provide.
- The only trace is `health.last_error` on the routine row. Nothing raises it, and the claim-refusal text an agent sees says only "this floor CLEARS ON ITS OWN", which reads as normal operation.
- Latency silently doubles: every item rides the 60-minute backstop instead of the 30-minute screened path.

So during any account-starvation window, duplicate screening across the workspace is quietly OFF while continuing to look on. That is the same defect class this tree treats as first-order everywhere else — a bounded/failed instrument whose output is indistinguishable from a real result.

Worth noting as a plausible instance rather than a proven one: I minted **four duplicate consults** on one plan earlier today. I have not established a causal link and am not claiming one; it is the kind of outcome this failure mode would produce.

## Suggested fix, in preference order

1. **Make the degradation loud.** When the promoter's tick fails, emit/alert rather than only stamping `health.last_error`. A silently fail-open screening gate is the whole bug.
2. **Distinguish the two admissions the census cannot.** `unreviewed` currently conflates "screened and found clean" with "never screened, admitted by timeout". `admitted_by = FAIL_OPEN_ACTOR` already carries the truth — surface it wherever admission state is read, so a fail-open backlog is visible as one.
3. **Survive partial starvation.** A per-item try/catch with backoff would let a tick screen what it can instead of losing the whole batch to the first usage-limit rejection.

## Reproduction

Starve the account the `system:work-item-admission-promoter` role routes through, then file an unassigned work-item and watch: the promoter tick errors, the item sits `pending` for the full 60 minutes, and is then admitted `unreviewed` by `FAIL_OPEN_ACTOR` having never been screened.

## Note on this filing

Filed unassigned, so this item will itself sit in the `pending` queue it describes — a usable end-to-end check of the behaviour above.

_claimSubjectBaseline.body:
## Observation (measured, not inferred)
- The shared QEMU VM serving the windows smoke rig on 127.0.0.1:2223 has been UP 12 days 18 hours, continuously consuming ~8 vCPUs.
- Its sshd NEVER answers: the connection reaches banner exchange and times out. The PORT IS LISTENING, so any probe that checks reachability rather than a completed handshake reads it as healthy.
- The mac rig on :2222 answers but REJECTS the provisioned `papercup-vm-mac` key.
- Host context: `/` is at 99% (35 GB free of 1.9 TB) and this box runs the whole agent fleet. 8 cores burned continuously for 12+ days is a large invisible tax on every other lane.

## Two distinct defects, deliberately not conflated
1. **The VM is wedged and nobody noticed for 12+ days.** A LISTENING port with a never-completing handshake is the worst available failure shape: invisible to a port probe, surfacing only when someone needs it — which is always mid-release.
2. **There is no detector.** Nothing alarms on a QEMU guest pegging N cores for days, and nothing alarms on a smoke rig that has served no successful run in N days. The second is the one that matters — this is a DETECTOR FAILURE, not merely a wedged process.

## Consequence for releases
The platform-smoke gate is the ONLY gate that exercises an INSTALLED artifact. Provenance and signatures prove the bytes are the bytes we built and signed; they prove nothing about whether the installer RUNS. With the rig wedged, every release since it died has had to override that gate — and an override that is unavoidable every single time stops being a decision and becomes a formality.

## Correction to a claim I was carrying (on the record as FALSE)
I nearly justified the override with a carried note saying the build VM is retired. That was FALSE. WI-5651 retired those VMs as BUILD legs; the SMOKE rig is a separate thing, both ports are live, and a genuine 0.0.19 windows smoke receipt exists on disk from 2026-09-09. The correct justification is that the rig is WEDGED — an evidenced exception. Same override either way, but only one of the two is honest in a ship record.

## Evidence
- `ss -ltnp | grep 222` → :2222 and :2223 both LISTENING.
- `timeout 8 ssh -o BatchMode=yes -p 2223 -i ~/.ssh/papercup-vm-win user@127.0.0.1 true` → timeout at banner exchange; no auth attempt reached.
- The 0.0.21-alpha ship record carries this verbatim as the smoke-gate override reason (/tmp/upload-real.log).

## Durable fix (not just a restart)
Restart/rebuild the guest (recovers 8 cores) and re-provision the mac rig key — then add the MISSING DETECTOR: alarm when a smoke rig has served no successful run in N days, so the gate cannot silently decay again. A restart alone leaves the trap armed.

_claimSubjectBaseline.body: Suspected operator event-loop defect: an earlier dev:service_health sample recorded :3070 accept backlog 45/511 and a 3011ms probe timeout while the systemd unit remained active; the same sample recorded majorFaultDelta=0, memory PSI full=0 and swap=0, followed by HTTP 200 and nRestarts=0. New targeted papercusp-dev-api.service logs show the sentinel reported STALLED at 02:58:57.896Z after 10,018ms (main thread spinning, state R, 0.99 cores, CPU PSI some60=5.4), then SIGKILLed request-worker PID 2970199 at 02:59:11.910Z after 24,031ms (mode kill, 20,000ms threshold, 0.98 cores, PSI=5.77). At 02:59:22 a PAPERCUSP_BACKGROUND_WORKERS=0 secondary host booted; the live systemd operator unit nRestarts=0 supports worker respawn without a unit restart, so the title remains accurate. Same-window bounded-timeout lines for turn-start executable frontier and agent-obligations show slow work but do not identify a caller; system journal had no OOM/hung-task/lockup matches. This establishes a nearby request-worker CPU-spin class, not exact linkage to the earlier 02:57 sample or the JS frame. The prior carry-note statement that 02:50–03:05Z had zero service-journal entries was wrong. The worker is gone, so its JS stack cannot be recovered. No code change is justified from this trace alone: on the next recurrence, act on the first STALLED line (~10s stale), send SIGUSR1 to the reported Node PID, capture /json/list and a 3–5s V8 sampling profile before the 20s kill threshold, plus per-thread /proc state/wchan/cgroup and unit+system journals. See agent-insights/profiling-a-wedged-node-host-runbook.

_claimSubjectBaseline.body:
Observed 2026-10-05 ~20:20Z while running the grading-integrity audit of EI-25171788938691287 (audit EI-25172375455718591, judge session su-b50e85cc).

The graded card's prefer-structured-check evidence pins its proof to a commit: 'Reproduce via git show 9e2fba799e7d4c0bd426415e9834c2cf3bd4f8ab:<path>'. It also claims the current bytes of all 10 bound test paths equal that commit's blobs. The grading-integrity rubric's re-runnable-evidence drill says to 'execute each evidence probe exactly as written', and the kickoff brief says 'Preserve the stored evidence scope; do not substitute a newer working tree'.

The judge-scoped MCP principal ('system:judge') is refused every read-only route to commit-pinned content:
- capability:git → missing_capability (show / rev-parse / hash-object all unavailable)
- dev:pg_query → missing_capability intel:read
- dev:pipeline_position → role_not_allowed (judge is not on the allowlist)

So the auditor can only read the WORKING TREE with capability:read, which is exactly the substitution the brief forbids. In this audit, three consult-routing-health.test.ts titles cited at :168/:205/:214 sit at :173/:207/:216 in the working tree. Whether that is drift after the commit or a citation error could not be determined: the commit could not be read.

Proposed fix (smallest extension, reuse-first): grant the judge role a read-only git subset (show <sha>:<path>, rev-parse <sha>:<path>, hash-object <path>, log -1 -- <path>) on capability:git. Alternatively, add judge to dev:pipeline_position's allowlist and expose a commit-blob read there. Either way, grade-the-grader audits could then honour commit-pinned evidence scope. No write capability is needed.

So the auditor can only read the WORKING TREE with capability:read, which is exactly the substitution the brief forbids. In this audit, three consult-routing-health.test.ts titles cited at :168/:205/:214 sit at :173/:207/:216 in the working tree. Whether that is drift after the commit or a citation error could not be determined: the commit could not be read.

Proposed fix (smallest extension, reuse-first): grant the judge role a read-only git subset (show <sha>:<path>, rev-parse <sha>:<path>, hash-object <path>, log -1 -- <path>) on capability:git. Alternatively, add judge to dev:pipeline_position's allowlist and expose a commit-blob read there. Either way, grade-the-grader audits could then honour commit-pinned evidence scope. No write capability is needed.

_claimSubjectBaseline.body:
Observed 2026-10-05 ~21:30Z while running the grading-integrity audit of EI-25176403929067237 (judge session, system:judge principal, build 8bb88cd105).

Symptom: the card's only evidenceRefs were thread-post:1158166 (6679 chars) and thread-post:1158172 (7013 chars). Reading them was much harder than it should be:
1. conversations:get {id:'thread-post:1158166'} via tools:invoke returned post.body cut to ~1100 chars plus a scratch-page cursor ("[TRUNCATED +5879 chars]").
2. capability:read {file_path:<that scratch .md>, raw:true} refused with scratch_line_window_too_large, because the spill is one JSON line. The documented alternative is byte pages of base64, which a model cannot read directly.
3. code:run returning body.slice() chunks still had each string capped at ~400 chars ("[truncated 1104 chars]"). One run returning 10x380 chars spilled again to a papercusp.output-envelope/v1 (shared result-door budget).
4. What worked: 8 sequential code:run calls, each returning 5x380-char windows. Two posts took 8 model turns.

Why it matters: every grading-integrity auditor of a meta-acceptance-rubric attestation has to read these consult critique posts, which are routinely ~7k chars, so this cost repeats on every audit.

Proposed fix (either one):
(a) conversations:get accepts {bodyOffset, bodyLimit} (or bodyWindow) for thread-post refs, so a reader can page the body as plaintext; or
(b) capability:read raw:true on a single-line scratch spill splits that line into plaintext char windows (offset/limit by chars) instead of refusing.
Option (b) fixes every tool's spills, not just conversations:get.

Unconfirmed: whether a superuser (non-judge) session gets a larger per-field cap.

terminalCompletionEvidence.summary: Fixed disclosed-gap loss when an evidence binding is re-appended without new proof. The evaluator now carries a prior disclosure while the active logical reference retains the same proof identity, and while a changed proof is not server-current. Added coverage for same-proof persistence and for closing the gap with a new testRunId or source fingerprint.
terminalCompletionEvidence.testResult: Focused file passed 111/111 at local HEAD f7abe91dfd; the new same-proof test failed before the source fix with disclosed-gap not-applicable, and passed after it. The focused run exercised local source and test edits; it did not verify a deployed runtime.
terminalCompletionEvidence.verifiedHow: Current runtime evidence showed bindings 23753 and 23762 share testRunId 20700025 and identical fingerprints, while only 23753 carried disclosedGap; the pre-fix evaluator rated that criterion not-applicable. The post-fix unit test retains the gap for identical proof and allows closure in both new-proof controls. git diff --check passed.

rootCauseVerification.hypothesis: activeSpecEvidence collapses binding history by logical clause/evidence reference, while disclosed-gap grading reads only the projected row; a metadata-only rebind therefore erased a disclosure from the same immutable proof.
rootCauseVerification.testResult: Before the fix the identical-proof case rated not-applicable. After the fix it rated fail and blocked; both changed-proof controls rated not-applicable. The focused suite passed 111/111.
rootCauseVerification.actualObservation: Runtime binding rows 23753 and 23762 had the same testRunId 20700025 and identical fingerprints; only 23753 had the disclosed gap. The pre-fix evaluation selected 23762 and rated disclosed-gap not-applicable, while the overall verdict was unknown for separate criteria. The pre-fix regression matched this result and the post-fix suite passed.
rootCauseVerification.distinguishingTest: Grade two bindings for one exact clause and logical evidence reference with identical testRunId, coverage reference, and fingerprints, where only the older row has disclosedGap; compare with controls where the active row changes testRunId or source fingerprint.
rootCauseVerification.alternativeHypothesis: The current data contained genuinely new server-current proof that superseded the older disclosure, or the disclosed row was absent from the exact clause evidence population.

predictedObservations.hypothesis: The identical-proof pair keeps the older gap and blocks; a changed server-current proof without a gap closes it.
predictedObservations.alternativeHypothesis: The identical-proof pair returns not-applicable because the newest binding alone determines disclosure state; the runtime row pair differs in proof identity or lacks an exact active predecessor.

Re-runnable evidence:
1. plans:get-spec-evidence {harness:'papercusp', slug:'cloud-dashboard-stripe-test-rollout-2026-10-03', specIds:['AUTO-BAR-R-1-P-001'], detail:'full'} → 4 bindings, all currentness=current. Binding 23753 (WI-10005828, 2026-10-03T12:53:27Z) has evidenceRef 'test-run-group:27fc109b-8102-46c5-b201-23068af16109:0' and testRunId 20700025. Its details.adequacy.disclosedGap = 'Registered injected Stripe account/offer unit controls; deployed account independently verified. Commercial metering remains outside approved scope.' Binding 23762 (13:07:22Z) has the SAME evidenceRef, the same testRunId and identical source/test fingerprints. It has NO disclosedGap and adds the fixtureCalibrated and oracleIndependent flags. Binding 23747 is a third copy.
2. plans:evaluate-spec-test-adequacy {harness:'papercusp', slug:'cloud-dashboard-stripe-test-rollout-2026-10-03', classRef:'plan-class-feature-ship', specIds:['AUTO-BAR-R-1-P-001'], specRevision:2, specFingerprint:'0f8323ea2c629d7effcda0a99cbe2f1a9d6f799a7f1516fc3535ae4885bbd59a', replaySnapshot:true, includeDraft:true, detail:'full'} (UNSCOPED, no evidenceRefs pin) → selects only bindings 23769 and 23762. It returns disclosed-gap 'not-applicable' with evidence 'No bound proof … records a disclosed gap', clause verdict 'pass', wouldBlock [].

Why this is a bug: the spec-test-adequacy rubric (rev 6) disclosed-gap drift marker explicitly lists 'a gap treated as mitigated by re-binding without closing it'. Here a re-bind with no new run erases an author disclosure from the machine verdict. The emitted evidence string also does not say that current bindings were excluded.

Mechanism UNCONFIRMED [inferred]: the evaluator appears to keep only the latest binding per (workItem, spec, revision, evidenceRef). I could not read the source because the judge principal lacks intel:read for code:structural and dev:pg_query.

Suggested fix: make disclosed-gap read adequacy.disclosedGap across every current binding of the clause, or carry a disclosure forward until a binding with NEW evidence (a different testRunId or fingerprint) explicitly closes it. Name the excluded or superseded binding ids in the evidence string.

Related (not the same issue): EI-24815130936541168 (disclosedGap read only from details.adequacy) and EI-24159008584241244 (dirty runs counted as durable). The sibling card EI-25199581201461275 on the same clause passed its audit (EI-25199769430569899) and may share this defect; I did not check it.

At ~2026-10-07T10:13Z, during the grading-integrity audit of EI-25314637985691697, a tools:invoke -> improvements:capture call returned from the papercusp MCP proxy: 'the operator process serving this tools/call died before it finished (upstream connection lost mid-response). The call was dispatched, so its effects are UNKNOWN'. A follow-up work_items:list {q:"omits detail:'full'", createdSince:'2026-10-07T10:00:00Z'} showed the write HAD committed (EI-25315118858899766). Context: a scorecards:emit 1 min earlier reported gradedGeneration.staleHost:true (deployedSha 05503a13ff, bootHeadSha 33287a0d), so this was probably a deploy- or restart-driven restart. If it was a planned restart, the drain did not cover an in-flight tools/call. If it was not planned, it was a crash. Either way the caller cannot tell whether a non-idempotent write landed.

_claimSubjectBaseline.body:
Unrelated handlers lose output when the shared result-door projection requires overflow persistence but cannot write the scratch spill. EI-25408351848678899 reports an unavailable checkpoint cursor with spill-write-failed; EI-25409580348208359 and EI-25409749057195100 report explicit 30000ms ETIMEDOUT failures on document results; EI-25409763444620761 reports the same failure on directed mail. EI-25410024981236879 and EI-25410269323486697 instead receive empty output_spill_failed envelopes. The same post-handler failure affects mutations: EI-25410122061838770 retains a recorded receipt but loses canonical output, while EI-25410344016199089 confirms a committed emit whose receipt was entirely swallowed behind retryable:true. Repairing the shared persistence/fallback path addresses these manifestations together. Filesystem contention, disk pressure and writer serialization remain unverified; successfully written spills that cannot be read because of single-line truncation are a separate cause.

Different handlers reach the same post-handler result-door scratch writer, then report spill-write-failed/output_spill_failed, commonly ETIMEDOUT after 30000ms. Coordination threads (EI-25424920546318879), document reads (EI-25425159282204609), and transcript tails (EI-25425669800696149) lose overflow without a recoverable cursor. Capture and send mutations retain committed receipts but lose remaining output (EI-25423907483948308, EI-25424167976820667). EI-25423748222711260 shows the delayed variant: a roughly 6KB spill is still pending at the deadline, returns ENOENT immediately, and becomes readable later. EI-25426355936196935 links one failing invocation to scratch quota-wait with pendingWrites=121 and recoveryActive=true; this does not prove the storage cause of every occurrence. Repair the shared persistence, readiness, and recovery path while preserving mutation outcomes separately from projection failures.

admissionDeltaSweep.reason: Multiple current readers lose or cannot promptly recover overflow at the same result-door persistence boundary. Repeated 30-second failures support one shared mechanism; the lower-level storage cause remains unknown.

_claimSubjectBaseline.body:
Bounded tool output relies on the shared result door persisting omitted bytes to scratch. That persistence boundary fails or stalls across unrelated readers: EI-25428565685267666 loses 31 journal entries after a 30000ms spill timeout; EI-25430509822980671 loses activity rows with an unavailable spill-write-failed cursor; EI-25428890465793101 reports output_spill_failed for checkpoint reads and unavailable schema overflow. EI-25428645932897748 shows a 5.3KB scorecard spill exceeding the same deadline, although its file becomes readable later, demonstrating delayed recovery rather than permanent loss in that case. EI-25428617195110357 corroborates the shared persistence/recovery boundary. Repair spill settlement and lossless overflow recovery without attributing these failures to /tmp exhaustion, quota, contention or event-loop load absent measurement.

Shared-root-cause evidence: Multiple current readers lose or cannot promptly recover overflow at the same result-door persistence boundary. Repeated 30-second failures support one shared mechanism; the lower-level storage cause remains unknown.

report.message: request_rejected: superuser_native_session_verifier_unavailable during the before-batch run authority refresh.

_claimSubjectBaseline.body:
This item concerns intermittent failure of admin transaction startup during native session verification. The MCP rejection itself is the intentional security boundary: preserve fail-closed verification; do not admit an inherited or unverified native identity.

The original reporter recurrence was captured on 2026-10-09 against b7937697dc. A second encounter occurred during bulk-4903eb58-a140-4b78-b5da-8816ad1309f1 after four allowed acknowledgements and a 100-item recommendation batch. The transcript shows tools:invoke calling inbox:bulk-run-manifest and receiving request_rejected: superuser_native_session_verifier_unavailable before any further bulk report/action. The bulk pass subsequently completed through the sanctioned same-owner CLI route; that route's success alone did not establish native-wrapper health.

The exact second failure is tool_invocations:35038620 at 2026-10-10T01:04:07.336Z, coord owner su-7f5e54d1-974b-4603-9aeb-4cf2487f2a1d, serving process linux:b8c61f1d-f67c-43a8-ac9d-2286713e224f:38294679, build a2c76aa503. Its retained mcpAuthFailure is contextVerified=false, with carrier meta:threadId, candidateAdvSessionId=null and valueFingerprint=51d40c49bf5903be8bfae7dc1bbcf951855c4dc1c0ea365275222fc6c41ee1e0. verifierFailure.name=DbCallDeadlineError; phase=transaction_setup; acquisition.label=boundedOrgTxn:begin(admin); pool=org-admin; deadlineMs=7500; elapsedMs=7499; retryable=true. No PostgreSQL error code was retained. verifierFailure.durationMs=201 is a separate measurement from the deadline object's elapsedMs; the record does not establish that this verifier call itself waited 7499ms. The captured pool/ticket counts are seam diagnostics, not evidence of CPU/RAM exhaustion or a saturated pool.

Current-runtime read-only probe: invoke the same manifest read through the native tools:invoke wrapper, using this session's ordinary metadata. It succeeded at 2026-10-10T01:31:59.128Z/129Z, receipts tool_invocations:35052893 (inner) and 35052894 (wrapper). Both have the EXACT SAME serving process, build a2c76aa503, carrier and native-session fingerprint as the failure, and now show binding=bound, candidateAdvSessionId=39357. adv_sessions:39357 belongs to this Codex owner and started at 2026-10-10T00:46:42.032456Z, before the failure. This establishes current binding and identity continuity; it does not retroactively authorize the rejected call. A fresh failure did not reproduce, so reproduced=true is not claimed.

Security/source check: _mcp-host.ts:1880-1896 rejects on verifier exceptions to prevent the inherited-session authorization bug. The existing registered gating suite covers fail-closed rejection, no terminal callback dispatch, redacted diagnostics, and typed acquire/begin/setup deadline fields. Focused test run 20966201 in papercusp/local passed five selected cases; 328 cases were deliberately excluded by the name filter. Command: npm run test:file -- --require-ran packages/operator-core/lib/endpoint-route/__tests__/mcp-handler-gating-matrix.test.ts -- '--testNamePattern=fails closed with a retryable verifier reason|retains typed .* deadline diagnostics when native verification fails closed'. The unused --require-ran token was treated as a non-test input; actual matched cases and counts are verified in testing:runs. HEAD moved 6fa9ff1f727d to b20fd572c871 during the run, runtime source capture was not configured, and the runner/ledger marked provenance unknown/worktreeDirty=true. These are exploratory guard observations, not build-bound acceptance evidence.

Remaining work: determine why boundedOrgTxn:begin(admin) failed, correlate the relevant verifier request/ticket with transaction/connection diagnostics from that serving process, and establish a durable fix with source-bound regression evidence. The existing current-process completed-query ring does not cover in-flight/acquisition/non-ReadyForQuery failures and cannot substitute for the incident's missing causal trace. The underlying database/startup cause remains unverified. No code change, restart, deadline widening, retry bypass or auth weakening was made. Keep the issue open; no fixed/shipped claim.

terminalCompletionEvidence.summary: Pinned the shared Linux papercusp-server.service to the dedicated systemd inference gateway as the sole :8788 authority; confirmed the prior bind-conflict stream stopped after the server loaded the override.
terminalCompletionEvidence.testsRun: apps/operator/scripts/__tests__/bghost-bundled-entry.test.ts: 10/10 passed in the prior checkpoint; not rerun during this continuation.
terminalCompletionEvidence.verifiedHow: Systemd reports the papercusp-server drop-in loaded and its process environment has PAPERCUSP_GATEWAY_SUPERVISE=0. The :3271 operator and MCP handshake both return 200. The dedicated inference gateway is active/healthy with zero probe failures, restartsLast10m=0, flapState=ok, and the aggregate unhealthy-supervision count is 0. The :8788 listener is in the dedicated gateway process tree. Gateway logs show 73 EADDRINUSE entries from 05:18:48.460Z through 07:24:56.564Z, all before the server's 07:27:46Z activation with the override, and none afterward.

rootCauseVerification.hypothesis: The packaged papercusp-server fallback and the dedicated systemd inference gateway competed to bind :8788, causing repeated EADDRINUSE failures in the dedicated gateway.
rootCauseVerification.testResult: pass: the bind-conflict stream stopped after the server loaded the override, and current ownership and health match the single-gateway hypothesis.
evidenceRefs: EI-25571977771070378 checkpoint: prior focused contract test result, 10/10
dev:service_health: papercusp-server.service and papercup-inference-gateway.service; :3271 operator/MCP 200; supervisionUnhealthy=0
systemctl --user show + ss -ltnp + ps: PAPERCUSP_GATEWAY_SUPERVISE=0 and :8788 listener in gateway process tree
rootCauseVerification.testProcedure: Read papercusp-server.service and papercup-inference-gateway.service journals over the bounded four-hour window with an EADDRINUSE filter; compare log timestamps to the server ActiveEnterTimestamp; inspect systemd Environment/MainPID, the :8788 listener PID and parent chain, and dev:service_health.
rootCauseVerification.actualObservation: The dedicated gateway journal had 73 EADDRINUSE rows from 2026-10-10T05:18:48.460Z to 07:24:56.564Z, all before the server's 07:27:46Z activation; there were zero such rows afterward. The current server process has PAPERCUSP_GATEWAY_SUPERVISE=0. The gateway unit is active/healthy with zero probe failures and flapState=ok, and its process tree owns the :8788 listener.
rootCauseVerification.distinguishingTest: Timestamp-correlate EADDRINUSE entries from both service units with the server activation that loaded the host-only override; then verify the effective server process environment, :8788 listener process ancestry, and current service health.
rootCauseVerification.alternativeHypothesis: The dedicated inference gateway failed independently while no competing server fallback was binding :8788.

predictedObservations.hypothesis: EADDRINUSE entries occur while the server fallback is enabled and stop after PAPERCUSP_GATEWAY_SUPERVISE=0 is loaded; the dedicated gateway owns :8788 and becomes healthy.
predictedObservations.alternativeHypothesis: The dedicated gateway continues failing after the server override is active, or the bind-conflict records do not stop at the server activation boundary.

_claimSubjectBaseline.body:
Measured 2026-10-11 ~00:33Z during grading-integrity audit EI-25641212024088928 of spec-test-adequacy card EI-25640783139681422.

Grading-audit kickoff briefs say "Preserve the complete bytes for the cited blob's integrity check". The spec_evidence_bindings.details.measurementPin.files[] rows carry sha256 + headBlob per file. Two examples: binding 35658 pins packages/operator-core/lib/code-intelligence/lsp-daemon-cache.test.ts at sha256 c211755e…, headBlob d5ff3c76…; binding 35687 pins native-ecosystem.test.ts at sha256 8769cc98….

Neither instrument available to a judge can produce a comparable hash:
1. capability:git-evidence { op:'readFileAtCommit' } returns only { ok, op, commitSha, path, bytes, content, _meta }. It has no blob oid and no sha256.
2. code:run has no `crypto` global. Calling `crypto.subtle.digest('SHA-256', …)` threw "crypto is not defined", so the script cannot hash the content itself.
The judge role is also told not to use capability:git or shell. So the blob-to-pin identity can only be taken on trust from server-measured currentness, and the audit has to record that as a gap.

Proposed fix (smallest extension, no new surface): have readFileAtCommit also return `blobOid` (git's own object id) and `sha256` of the returned bytes. Alternatively or additionally, expose a `sha256(string|Uint8Array)` helper in the code:run sandbox. Either one lets an auditor compare directly against measurementPin.files[].sha256/headBlob.

Related: scorecards:get criterion evidence pages are ~2.9KB each (EI-25632408471242790 already tracks that). This audit worked around it by reading the payload via dev:pg_query on harness_shared.work_items.payload->'observation'->'ratings'.

ⓘ Possible STALE RUNTIME, not an open defect: `packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools` (4 newer commits, tip `9b9e9ae5f8390f9191b31faf0fa06a0845619540`) have commits newer than the running build (`3e02a3af06`) in `staging`. If this was observed live, verify the deployed generation before triaging; the behavior may already be fixed in the tree.

Neither instrument available to a judge can produce a comparable hash:
1. capability:git-evidence { op:'readFileAtCommit' } returns only { ok, op, commitSha, path, bytes, content, _meta }. It has no blob oid and no sha256.
2. code:run has no `crypto` global. Calling `crypto.subtle.digest('SHA-256', …)` threw "crypto is not defined", so the script cannot hash the content itself.
The judge role is also told not to use capability:git or shell. So the blob-to-pin identity can only be taken on trust from server-measured currentness, and the audit has to record that as a gap.

Proposed fix (smallest extension, no new surface): have readFileAtCommit also return `blobOid` (git's own object id) and `sha256` of the returned bytes. Alternatively or additionally, expose a `sha256(string|Uint8Array)` helper in the code:run sandbox. Either one lets an auditor compare directly against measurementPin.files[].sha256/headBlob.

Related: scorecards:get criterion evidence pages are ~2.9KB each (EI-25632408471242790 already tracks that). This audit worked around it by reading the payload via dev:pg_query on harness_shared.work_items.payload->'observation'->'ratings'.

_claimSubjectBaseline.body:
OBSERVED 2026-10-11 ~00:59Z (judge su-94c69eb9, grading-integrity audit of EI-25641605517480359): a successful tools:invoke { name:'scorecards:emit' } (completionReceipt recorded, effectRef EI-25642361636963872) came back with _projection.cursor.kind='volatile-scratch-page', reason='spill-write-failed', errorCode='ETIMEDOUT', errorDetail='Error: result-door scratch spill write exceeded 30000ms'. The payload was only 8796 chars. A 30s+ write for a ~9KB spill points to blocked or contended scratch persistence, not payload size. Unconfirmed cause.

Same session, related degraded signals: (a) code:run returns were repeatedly spilled with accounting.summaryBudgetChars=0 and incomplete.reason='aggregate-output-budget-exceeded' / 'under-budget-partial-result' (recoverable:false) for ~6KB summaries, apparently because of concurrent grading-audit judges sharing one result-door budget cohort. (b) Every turn's memory leg timed out, and the query embed exceeded its ~297ms budget.

Impact: the emit is non-idempotent, and the only exact copy of its result lived in an in-process volatile URI that expires in ~15 min and is lost on restart. A caller who cannot read it must reconstruct the outcome from the ledger. Load-correlated (≈400 live peers, many concurrent judges). Expected: a spill of under 10KB persists within the deadline at any load.

_claimSubjectBaseline.body:
MEASURED 2026-10-11T09:33Z judging WI-6554700010008504 (task 0mv2kuyk2ctvxu6p7qd, unaccounted-residue).

The task_ledger row for this kernel residue is a reconciler-synthesized stub:
  argv = []  (jsonb, empty)   cwd = null   log_path = null   launched_by = "unknown"
  session_id = null, parent_task_id = null, work_item_id = null, plan_slug = null, fleet_slug = null
  title = 200 chars, hard-truncated mid-path: "... systemd-scope-env-runner.mjs --env-fd-path /proc/self/fd/3 -- /home/marsh-office/"

The process is a systemd-scope-env-runner.mjs shim whose entire purpose is to exec an INNER command after the "--". That inner command is the only thing identifying what this residue is. It is truncated away in title, absent from argv, and processes:list exposes no argv/command/cmdline field at all (measured task key set has none).

CONSEQUENCE: the keep/kill judgment turns on whether this is an abandoned rig or a legitimately idle long-lived sidecar — it sits in papercusp-sidecar.slice with 0 CPU for 17.5h, which is normal for an idle sidecar AND consistent with abandonment. With the inner command unrecoverable that question is unanswerable from any available instrument, forcing a perpetual "keep". /proc/<pid>/cmdline is no fallback: capability:bash runs in a separate PID namespace (measured $$=2, 5 visible numeric /proc entries, ns pid:[4026543257]), so host PIDs are invisible there.

SUGGESTED CHANGE: when the reconciler synthesizes a ledger row for an unenrolled pc-*.scope, capture /proc/<pid>/cmdline into argv (and /proc/<pid>/cwd into cwd) at discovery time from the host-visible reconciler context, storing full argv rather than relying on a truncated title. That single field makes an unaccounted-residue verdict decidable instead of indefinitely deferred.

_claimSubjectBaseline.body:
UNCONFIRMED CAUSE — the observation is filed; the mechanism is not proven.

What I saw: during the grading-integrity audit of scorecard EI-25828255998725711 (judge session su-628f4d8c, client papercusp-su via tools:invoke), two read-only code:run calls returned {error:'mcp_proxy_upstream_error', forwardingResult:'outcome_unknown', detail:'read ECONNRESET', attempts:1, windowMs:90000}. traceIds: 27cc7b31-c7d1-481a-9f1d-a9720b184a9f (~2026-10-13T02:10:49Z) and 0c98adaa-8afa-4744-be9d-03bf179b469c (~02:12:10Z). Each script made 23-24 scorecards:get reads plus one plans:evaluate-spec-test-adequacy call. An identical retry succeeded both times. Afterwards the responses carried _dataPlaneMayBeDegraded warnings. A testing:runs error at ~02:13Z said build d740fc3802 had 'started 25min ago'. The scorecards:emit response at 02:16:10Z reported gradedGeneration.hostStartedAt=2026-10-13T02:14:09Z and staleHost=true. So the serving host apparently restarted between 02:13 and 02:14:09. That restart came AFTER both resets, so a restart does not obviously explain them.

Why it matters: outcome_unknown on a code:run means the caller cannot tell whether nested writes happened, so every agent has to reason about idempotency on each reset. A read-only audit can safely retry; a writing script cannot.

Probe: query harness_shared.tool_invocations for coord_owner_id su-628f4d8c-87ea-4d57-a493-58504e273aa3, tool_name code:run, between 02:10 and 02:13Z, and read serving_host / serving_build_sha / duration. Correlate that with the :9071 proxy log for the two traceIds and the operator journal for that window. Check whether long-running code:run (~25 nested dispatches) is hitting an upstream socket or idle timeout.

UNCONFIRMED. The root cause is not known; the timing link below is an inference.

Observed 2026-10-14 ~07:06-07:08Z by the grading-integrity judge (audit EI-25937822279694569 of card EI-25937267761663359). I made the same read three times: plans:get-spec-evidence { harness:'papercusp', slug:'consult-backed-parking-2026-10-12', specIds:['AUTO-BAR-R-21-P-007'], detail:'full' } (bindings 43554, 43555).
- Call 1 (code:run callId ubrxmz-k8x, elapsedMs 6208): both bindings returned currentness {"overall":"unknown","dimensions":{"spec":"current","source":"unknown","test":"unknown","fixture":…}. The output was truncated, and I did not capture unknownReasons.
- Call 2 (~1 min later): top-level currentness {current:2, stale:0, unknown:0}.
- Call 3 (callId ubrxmz-kbx, elapsedMs 111): both bindings overall:current, every dimension current, provenance server-measured, no stale/unknown reasons.
Nothing about the bindings changed in between (createdAt 06:57:11/12Z, no retraction).

Why it matters: a grader or auditor who takes the slow read reports freshness 'unknown' on proof that is current, so currentness is a function of server load rather than evidence. That is a false negative from a measuring instrument.

Hypothesis [inferred, not probed]: under load the server-side source/test fingerprint measurement times out or degrades to 'unknown' instead of retrying or surfacing a load reason. Probe: re-run the read while the operator is under concurrent load and compare currentness.unknownReasons with the elapsedMs of the same call. If the reason is a timeout or deadline, the unknown is load-induced and should carry a distinct reason such as measurement-deadline, not read as evidence-unknown.

Related (different tool, same class): EI-25931455671559212 (scorecards:get transient rubricCurrentness unknown under concurrent load). Result-door spill ETIMEDOUT also recurred about 8 times in this audit session (already filed as EI-25932014678052487).

Before diagnosing or fixing it, correlate both events with proxy/upstream logs or trace identifiers, or reproduce through the same route while recording the serving runtime and terminal outcome. Do not infer snapshot state or claim a root cause from these reports alone.

16 open orders; the carry excerpts of #127, #128, #130, #132, #134, #135 (self-compaction), #131, #133 (wake-pump) and #136, #137 (fleet-kickoff, recorded by role-* grading auditors) all begin `<pasted_content id=…>\n⟦turn-origin:…⟧` — i.e. machine-injected turns captured as owner directives, ~10 in ~20 minutes across ~9 sessions.

## Cause (measured in code)
`packages/operator-core/lib/turn-provenance/envelope-grammar.ts:67` — `ENVELOPE_PATTERN_SOURCE = ^\s*⟦turn-origin:(…) nonce:(…)⟧` is START-anchored; `parseEnvelope` (turn-provenance.ts:149) uses it, so a `<pasted_content …>` prefix defeats the match. `grep -rl pasted_content` over scripts/, packages/operator-core/lib, apps/operator/lib → 0 files: no code unwraps the wrapper. The ledger-hash fallback also misses (wrapped text ≠ injected payload), so classify() falls through to the final OWNER branch (turn-provenance.ts:671).
[inferred, not probed] The `<pasted_content>` wrapper is added by the Claude Code client when a long prompt is delivered as input; the injectors send a correctly-enveloped payload.

## Why major
1. Manufactures owner directives out of machine text (the WI-3532 failure class) and floods every session's Orientation with bogus PENDING directives that agents must resolve by hand.
2. The mode-registration hook is gated on this turn classifying OWNER — a wrapped machine turn containing AUTO/ideate phrasing could register a mode as ownerDirected:true.
3. Session search provenance (`turn_origin`) marks these turns owner-typed.

## Suggested durable fix
Unwrap a leading `<pasted_content id=…>` … `</pasted_content>` (and whatever other client wrappers exist) BEFORE envelope parse + ledger hash, in ONE shared normalizer used by all 4 grammar sites (see EI-20202332205249019 — the grammar is re-typed in 4 sites/3 languages, incl. the shell form at envelope-grammar.ts:93). Recurrence guard: a unit test in turn-provenance feeding a wrapped enveloped continuation and asserting VERIFIED AGENT-ORIGIN, plus a test that a wrapped owner paste without an envelope still classifies OWNER. Consider a one-shot sweep dismissing currently-open orders whose text starts with a wrapped envelope.

Related (different leak paths, both closed): WI-38268, WI-37908.

MEASURED 2026-09-26 (su-07b72cf6, for WI-10002524 / P-521, plan D-066).

Observation: nightly 0.0.22-20260926.1031 (task 0mui91l2w1pvzp6g1dh, green main 13342a27) passed migration boot-smoke (TEST_FILE_RESULT status=passed, 63s). It then died at 10:44:29Z with "==> seed: no committed corestore to reuse — cutting FRESH from the live store (requires a quiesced operator)" / "ERROR: fresh release seed cut requires a quiesced operator; run bin/cut-seed-quiesced.sh." (journalctl --user -u pc-0mui91l2w1pvzp6g1dh.scope).

Mechanism [measured by reading code]: papercusp-desktop/src-tauri/seed is gitignored (papercusp-desktop/.gitignore:61). apps/operator/bin/release/setup-release-checkout.sh extract_submodule_source does rm -rf $RELEASE_ROOT/<submodule> and re-extracts from git archive on every fire, so an isolated cut root NEVER has a seed snapshot. release-local.sh cut_release_seed (auto mode) then falls to the fresh-from-live-store branch. That branch requires release_seed_cut_is_quiesced (a runtime marker or masked bg-host), which a managed routine never has. This has never surfaced before: the 09-24 nightly died earlier at leg start (WI-10003216) and today's 07:00Z died at boot-smoke (WI-10003218).

Fix (su-07b72cf6): release-local.sh cut_release_seed hydrates src-tauri/seed from a persistent snapshot store (PAPERCUSP_SEED_SNAPSHOT_DIR, default ~/.papercusp/release-seeds/current; empty disables) when the root has no corestore. The existing auto-reuse path then refreshes git+epoch-keys only, with no quiesce needed. Populate the store from the newest quiesced cut (papercusp-relcut-0021-current seed, cutTs 2026-09-22T07:34Z).

Impact: every managed nightly and every isolated cut root fails here until fixed. This is the P-521 candidate blocker.

An earlier 5 s sample at 09:02Z: w_await 745 ms, aqu 441. D-019 (plan host-memory-reduction-2026-09-27) measured fdatasync ~500 ms per write on this disk vs ~0.6 ms on nvme1n1.
- nvme0n1 = TEAM TM8FPW002T (hwmon model string), 2 TB, ext4 root, 90% full (1.7T used / 194G avail), mounted without discard; fstrim.timer weekly, last run 2026-09-21. Temperature 54.9 C (not throttling).
- nvme1n1 = WD_BLACK SN850X HS 8000GB, xfs /mnt/data, 76% (1.8T free).
- [inferred] A DRAM-less 2 TB drive at 90% full with its SLC cache exhausted writes at native speed plus GC. That fits reads at 0.9 ms next to writes at 785 ms.

WHAT WRITES TO IT (sampled 09:02-09:05Z):
- Postgres: data_directory /var/lib/postgresql/18/main, 136 GB, pg_wal NOT separated. So every commit's WAL fdatasync queues behind the 785 ms write backlog. [inferred] This is a floor under the latency of every tool call.
- apps/operator/bin/release/dependency-generation.sh: `cp -a --reflink=auto node_modules` (15 GB). ext4 has no reflink, so it is a full 15 GB copy (pid in bg-host, 270 MiB/10 s, running 12+ min), plus a second copy of a generation inside the green-checkpoint scope. 8 generations sit in .papercusp/dependency-generations.
- Dirty page cache: 7.7 GB Dirty in /proc/meminfo, 6.2 GB of it charged to papercusp-bg-host.service.

- nvme0n1 and nvme1n1 use scheduler `none`, which ignores ioprio. So IOSchedulingClass=idle / ionice -c3 have no effect (kopia pid 3738236 is class idle, and it still reads at full rate).
- user@1000.service has DelegateControllers=cpu memory pids (its cgroup.subtree_control is 'cpu memory pids'). The io controller is not delegated, so IOWeight / IOReadBandwidthMax / IOWriteBandwidthMax in any user unit is silently ignored too.
- 19 installed user units depend on these settings (kopia-home-snapshot, kopia-snapshots, papercusp-db-backup, papercup-backup-health, docker-reclaim, tmp-scratch-reclaim, vitest-orphan-reaper, webkit-reaper, pc-estate-mirror, ...). Sources: apps/operator/scripts/systemd/*.service.

1. Move Postgres data (or at least pg_wal) to nvme1n1: stop PG, rsync, then a bind mount or data_directory change, start. Needs a PG restart window, so the owner decides (it stops every agent's DB access for the copy; 136 GB at ~1-2 GB/s is a few minutes if the source is read while PG is down).
2. Move the other write-heavy trees off root the way .gitnexus was moved (D-020, fstab bind mount): .papercusp/dependency-generations, and consider the scratch/log dirs. On xfs with reflink=1, `cp --reflink` between generations on the same fs becomes near-free. [inferred: check xfs reflink=1 with xfs_info first]
3. Make IO de-prioritisation real: (a) nvme0n1 scheduler mq-deadline (it honours ioprio classes since 5.14; builtin here), persisted by a udev rule; and/or (b) delegate io to user@.service (drop-in Delegate=cpu cpuset io memory pids, then daemon-reload + user-manager re-exec) so IO*BandwidthMax works (blk-throttle works with any scheduler). Measure w_await / IO PSI before and after; revert is one write.
4. Root at 90% on a DRAM-less drive: free space helps its GC. Consider a daily fstrim (or discard) on /.

Do NOT: stop kopia or the release pipeline by hand; both are legitimate jobs. The fix is placement and priority, not killing them.

_claimSubjectBaseline.body:
MEASURED 2026-09-30 on avi-test (pc-host-3daf37098c8096b5d9e0ac72-877db740-vm, r62b 0.0.21-p318r62b), serial console (.papercusp/scratch/avi-test-serial-r62b.txt), su-be77f2f5, P-318:
- 11:16:27Z GCE start. 11:18:04Z startup-script [workspace-host-bootstrap] phase:verify-release, 11:18:51Z phase:install-runtime, 11:19:21Z phase:migrate-database + phase:configure-service.
- papercusp-desktop.socket and papercusp-workspace.service were already active at 11:18:56Z, so desktop.start succeeded: papercusp-desktop@0-694-999 started 11:18:58Z (desktop 0f9dadb3, watch probe reached desktop.ready 11:19:11Z).
- 11:19:23Z the bootstrap restarted papercusp-workspace.service. papercusp-desktop@.service has BindsTo=papercusp-workspace.service, so systemd stopped the desktop first. The customer's desktop was gone 25 s after it opened. The bootstrap completed at 11:19:54Z.
- The same restart also ends any terminal or agent session the customer opened in that window [inferred from the unit stop; not separately measured].

Impact: after any reboot, whatever a customer opens in roughly the first 3 minutes is killed without explanation. 'Units active' is not a readiness signal, which also misled the P-318 r62b avi-test acceptance script.

Fix options: (a) skip the reinstall and restart on a boot where the installed release already matches the manifest (verify-release passes, same storage:current), and only restart when something actually changed; or (b) keep papercusp-workspace from accepting desktop or session starts until the bootstrap writes its completion marker. (a) also removes about 110 s of redundant work on every boot.

Not a P-318 shipment blocker [self-imposed judgement, su-be77f2f5]: the desktop works once the bootstrap completes, and the reboot plus desktop.start acceptance passes.

_claimSubjectBaseline.body: Observed 2026-10-01 by su-72d22e0c: a broad read-only `pgrep -af` matched peer launch commands and surfaced full kickoff text plus a possible `PAPERCUSP_KICKOFF_PROOF_TOKEN` assignment. Do not copy the observed value. Source measurement: `spawnHeadless` creates `launchEnv` containing `PAPERCUSP_KICKOFF_PROOF_PATH` and `PAPERCUSP_KICKOFF_PROOF_TOKEN`, then passes that same object to `buildConsoleOneliner`; `buildConsoleOneliner` serializes every env entry as `export KEY='value'` inside the `bash -lc` argument. The same `launchEnv` is already passed through `spawn(...,{env})`, so putting the proof material in argv is redundant. The proof is random per launch, its parent wait is capped at 30 seconds, and `cleanupKickoffProofRequest` unlinks the unique 0600 receipt path after the wait; therefore the specific observed token has no durable revocation surface and is unusable once that path is gone. The systemic defect is the argv exposure during the active launch window (and accidental ingestion into logs/LLM context), which can permit same-UID proof forgery before cleanup. Durable fix: keep the proof path/token out of the oneliner argv while preserving them in the child environment, audit the headless launch-only env boundary for any other values violating `ConsoleEnvelope.env`'s documented non-secret invariant, and add canonical `console-spawn` tests that assert proof path/token are absent from `[bin,...args]`, present only in the child env, and the native kickoff receipt still succeeds. This is the same secret-in-argv defect class previously fixed on other surfaces in WI-41140 and EI-21270327070599812, but this headless console-spawn path remains exposed.

_claimSubjectBaseline.body:
EI-23768242440859949 shipped a PROPOSE-ONLY channel: recurrence-escalation.ts phase 3 posts one audited `recurrence-evidence:` comment per item (<=5/tick; >=3 ledger rows from >=2 distinct reporters in 7d; open, unassigned, non-observation minor/nit). Severity is never written. The idea's central claim - that prior recurrence predicts later manual re-grades / slow assignment - was NOT falsified: no severity-change history existed at ship time (2026-10-01) and only 7 of 71 recent assigned items had >=2 prior ledger rows.

WHEN: after ~2 weeks of proposal comments exist (query coord_thread_posts WHERE body LIKE 'recurrence-evidence:%').
DO: for items that received a proposal, measure (a) fraction later manually re-graded upward vs. matched un-proposed minor/nit controls, (b) time-to-assignment vs. controls. Report precision of the 3-rows/2-reporters gate. Decide: keep propose-only, tighten thresholds, or design a reviewed auto-apply policy. Do NOT enable auto-apply without this measurement (the lifetime gate passed ~80% of the 232 open minor/nit items, so an unvalidated bulk apply is the severity-inflation failure).
REF: packages/operator-core/lib/harness/improvements/recurrence-escalation.ts (INSTANCE_EVIDENCE_* constants + comment block), readRecurringInstanceEvidence in packages/operator-core/lib/issue-occurrence-ledger.ts.

_claimSubjectBaseline.body:
EI-20115751074601731 durable disk-headroom probe: the filesystem containing PostgreSQL data path '/var/lib/postgresql/18/main' is 100% used (warn threshold 90%). A full shared root volume takes PostgreSQL down fleet-wide by preventing WAL, lock, and data-directory writes.

trend: losing 0.63 GiB/h over the last 1.0h — ETA TO FULL ~7h at this rate

ACTION: inspect current filesystem consumers and free space before starting disk-heavy work. This probe is detection-only; it never deletes files or restarts PostgreSQL.

df output:
/dev/nvme0n1p2  1966788624 1941918128   4861160     100% /

LARGEST RELATIONS RIGHT NOW (read at alert time, not written down — see below):
  39.53 GiB  harness_shared.session_archive_files
  18.21 GiB  harness_shared.session_turns
  16.06 GiB  harness_shared.tool_invocations
  11.84 GiB  harness_shared.session_turn_chunks
  9.89 GiB  harness_shared.coord_thread_posts
  6.95 GiB  harness_shared.session_turn_parts

A relation flagged LIKELY TOAST BLOAT is the cheapest win available and needs no owner
decision: its bytes are almost entirely dead TOAST pages that plain VACUUM can never
return to the OS. Confirm by comparing pg_total_relation_size(reltoastrelid) against the
live payload (sum a denormalized length column, or sample pg_column_size), then reclaim
with a rewrite. ALWAYS bound the lock, because a rewrite takes ACCESS EXCLUSIVE and a
blocked one queues AHEAD of every later lock request on that table:
  sudo -n -u postgres env PGOPTIONS='-c lock_timeout=10000' psql -p 5432 -d papercusp \
    -c 'VACUUM (FULL, VERBOSE, ANALYZE) <schema>.<relation>'
Measured 2026-09-02 (WI-2140986): that reclaimed 60.89 GiB from gateway_payload_blobs in
55s with no contention and no data loss.

INVESTIGATION RECIPE (traps verified while working WI-38595, 2026-08-14, and WI-2141004, 2026-09-02):
1. PostgreSQL is usually NOT the consumer, despite this alarm's title — but "not PostgreSQL" is a HYPOTHESIS TO TEST, never a conclusion to inherit. The probe watches the VOLUME holding PGDATA, and that volume is shared with $HOME. Size PGDATA with 'sudo -n du -xsh /var/lib/postgresql/18/main' — an unprivileged du prints a SILENT '4.0K' (permission denied) rather than an error, which reads as 'Postgres is tiny' for the wrong reason. Start from the LARGEST RELATIONS block above and from a fresh directory scan; do not start from any remembered figure, including one quoted in an older issue. This step used to carry a measured example here, and it went stale and misdirected three work-items for three weeks.
2. CONFIRM WHICH VOLUME a directory is on before reclaiming anything: 'findmnt -T <path>' or 'stat -c %d <path>'. On this box /tmp is a BIND MOUNT from a second physical disk, so deleting 136 GiB of stale /tmp scratch frees exactly nothing on the volume this alarm is about.
3. Enumerate consumers in ONE bounded backgrounded pass: 'nice -n 19 ionice -c3 du -x -d3 / | sort -hr > /tmp/scan-1.txt' (~7 min here). Re-run it later into scan-2.txt and DIFF the two — a diff of two snapshots is the only reliable attribution of NET growth per directory.
4. Do NOT attribute growth by mtime ('find -newermt'). It counts a file's WHOLE size when the file is merely touched, so a single live VM image reads as hundreds of GiB 'written' in 26h. Note also that qcow2 images grow monotonically and never return space the guest frees — and the .img suffix lies, so check the magic ('QFI\373' = qcow2).

claim_hold_release.condition: Actual shipped :3070 artifact contains release.ts retain support from commit 7c7c4a29231ea4e762a6fce1a7783baa5b52fc5d and loaded runtime source identity is verified; then re-place bounded native retain attribution verification.

_claimSubjectBaseline.body:
[measured 2026-10-14T02:33Z, harness_shared.tool_invocations, workspace papercusp-workspace, last 5h] locks:release: 482 ok, 44 invalid-input from 16 owners, first 2026-10-13T21:34:34Z, latest 02:32:15Z. All 44 have one cause, `Unrecognized key: "retain"`, and all were served by port-3070, build d740fc3802.

[measured] Source: posttooluse-locks-release.sh:592 and posttoolbatch-locks-release.sh:484 send {retain:true, native_edit_proof} to attribute a native edit made under an explicitly held lock. The packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/locks/release.ts blob carrying `retain` is on staging (6958ed5d1f, commit 7c7c4a2923, 2026-10-13T01:44Z). main and the deployed d740fc3802 both carry cea7db3c42, which has no retain support (grep marker retain_requires_native_edit_proof: staging 1, main 0, d740fc3802 0).

[measured, from source] The impact is bounded and by design: release.ts:88-94 sends no `paths`, so an operator that predates `retain` refuses the request and releases no lock. The explicit hold survives. What is lost is the native-edit attribution in the ledger, and each refusal adds an invalid-input row to tool error rates.

Close condition: after :3070 serves a build whose release.ts contains retain_requires_native_edit_proof (state:read deploy.3070.sha, then dev:pipeline_position { path:'packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/locks/release.ts' } -> positions.deployed:true), re-run the same tool_invocations query. The `Unrecognized key: "retain"` count after the deploy time should be 0, and ok release rows with attributed paths should appear. If refusals continue after deploy, reclassify this as a bug.

Residue of WI-6554700010011168 (comment 1179642 listed release-argument errors as residue).

MEASURED 2026-10-14 05:29Z (su-def821c4): `dpkg-deb -c` of the exact D-224 Linux Server .deb (sha256 96650914…, 11518 entries; listing banked at /mnt/data/offload/papercusp-private-release-evidence/su-def82/d224-linux-server-deb-listing.txt, sha256 cdf09308…) contains NO */prompts/* entries and 0 *.persona.md files. Durable fix: a build-time closure gate in the vm-release packaging that statically lists the prompt files each Server-role tool/route needs. It fails the build when a reachable prompt is pruned, or it marks the tool unavailable in the Server role with a clear refusal. _claimSubjectBaseline.body:
[observed] P-010a isolated candidate install (WI-6554700010012436), VM p010a, Papercusp Server 0.0.26 .deb built from deployed main d740fc3802 (sha256 in ~/.papercusp/evidence/p010a-lifecycle-20261014/package-sha256.txt).

`/usr/bin/ptool backup:snapshot_list --json '{}'` and `ptool backup:snapshot_create` both fail: `ptool: Cannot find package '@modelcontextprotocol/sdk' imported from /usr/lib/Papercusp Server/sidecar/scripts/ptool.mjs [83 connect attempt(s) over 119s: 83x other]` (evidence p2-product.txt).

[observed] `ls '/usr/lib/Papercusp Server/sidecar/node_modules/@modelcontextprotocol'` → No such file or directory. /usr/bin/ptool is a postinst-managed launcher exec'ing sidecar/bin/node sidecar/scripts/ptool.mjs. Source apps/operator/scripts/ptool.mjs dynamically imports @modelcontextprotocol/sdk/client/index.js, client/streamableHttp.js and types.js (lines ~2505, 3427-3428), so the sidecar staging/pruning step ships ptool.mjs without its runtime dependency.

[inferred, unverified] the sidecar node_modules pruning keeps only the operator's static import graph; a dynamic import() is not traced.

Impact: the documented admin CLI (and the product backup verb path through it) is unavailable on packaged installs; the 120s connect-retry loop also masks a module-resolution error as a connection failure (83x other).

Acceptance: the packaged sidecar includes @modelcontextprotocol/sdk (or ptool is bundled); a packaged-install check runs `ptool --help` / one read verb and fails the package build when it errors; ptool reports a module-resolution failure immediately instead of retrying it as a connect failure.

This continuation is managed self-compaction at09:11. This may be EXPECTED protection while unrelated self-compaction inference remains active, not a proven detector bug. If expected in-flight protection, document that precise bound and supported guaranteed continuation route with measured proof. No second loop, no fake loop-origin prompt/proof, no arbitrary SQL lifecycle mutation, no LIVE_GATE_OPS or gate monitoring, no restart of gate-coupled bg-host. Use canonical staging/manual locks, current-build isolated route for tests; preserve all main program work.

_claimSubjectBaseline.body:
[owner:Avi 2026-10-21 directive #2149] asked: can we use our code-intelligence tools to also enhance our relevancy router?

Measured today (su-611f037a): packages/operator-core/lib/consult/relevance-router.ts blends similarity 0.55 / verification 0.15 / authorship 0.15. Authorship (lines ~1283-1299) only fires when extractPathTokens finds a literal path in the question, and then matches it by ILIKE substring against payload->'paths' of the candidate's COMMITTED work-items. Over the last 30 days 263 of 3966 persisted routings (6.6%, consult_state, all workspaces) had any candidate with authorship > 0.

Proposal:
1. Resolve the question to code subjects, not just literal paths: identifiers -> defining files via lsp:query workspace_symbols / the graph index, plus explicit paths; optional 1-hop graph neighbourhood (callers/impact) at reduced weight.
2. Source authorship from what agents actually did: edit_attribution_ledger edits per owner per file (strong) and code reads/lsp/graph queries from tool_invocations (weak 'familiarity'), the same inputs deriveCodeWorkingSet uses. Count all-time (D-007), no recency term (D-001 structural rule), and keep simFloor so track record cannot promote an irrelevant agent (D-003).
3. Reuse in acceptance-grader selection: edit attribution also identifies implementers who must be excluded.
4. Evaluate offline first: replay persisted consult_state.routing snapshots with the new signal and compare rankings and no_qualified_responder rates before changing weights.

Needs a plan (several items: subject resolution, signal source, grader-exclusion reuse, offline eval, weight calibration).

_claimSubjectBaseline.body: Independent P-006 acceptance finding. In libs/generic/chat-cards/src/structured-results.tsx, the normal activate response fence at lines 101-104 checks current.current.activate === callback and current.current.resolve === host.resolve before mutating state. The catch branch at lines 105-107 checks only token/key/abort. If the host replaces activate while an earlier action promise is pending, then the obsolete callback rejects, catch can set the still-current result state to unavailable even though the replacement host remains authorized. This violates ITEM-P-006-CONTRACT@3 stale-result-resolution / late-callback fencing. Required recurrence guard: extend the exact DOM integration detector 'foreign revoked and stale references cannot reveal protected content or dispatch actions' with a stale thrown/rejected action callback after same-key host.activate replacement; verify current content remains and the replacement seam is not poisoned. Review-only lane: no implementation edit made.

(1) member-productivity: 28 closes / 440.3 active seat-hours = 0.064 per hour (7-day baseline 0.18); 40 of 57 members with >=2 active seat-hours closed nothing. The admitted frontier is not empty (~1,410 admitted unheld bug/change, raw SQL), so starvation does not explain it. Members hold 131 non-terminal items (1,149 claimed-but-unclosed item-hours), 55 blocked (45 runtime live-dependency). (2) member-liveness: fleet:status 20:01Z shows 9 parked members, and loop:status on each reports active:false, rewakeGuaranteed:false (idle 15 min to 4.8h: su-d944f431, su-55e68e71, su-47ae7149, su-7f8aed23, su-6a3d50d5, a su-respawn-* member, 3 more). Leader made 0 coord:wake/dispatch calls in the window. (3) membership-churn: 9 member joins in 9.4h (~23/day vs target 50). Unknown cause: where member seat-time goes (repeat blocker reports are 64% of member messages per WI-6554700010029331) and why parked members lose their loop. Next: classify seat-time of the 40 zero-close members by tool family, and check why parked members' loops are inactive (loop ended vs never armed after respawn). Queries: .papercusp/scratch/feh/regrade-2000-batch1..5.json.

terminalCompletionEvidence.summary:
Removed the two stale ElevenLabs-CDN scratch pages from the committed sidecar staging SPA artifact, AND corrected this item's central claim: they were never shipped. The filed title said the SPA 'still ships' them; verification of the actual ship path shows no packaged artifact ever carried them. Corrected in full in the thread comment (post 79055).

Ship-path finding: the pages sat at the TOP-LEVEL papercusp-desktop/src-tauri/env-sidecars/staging/spa/. No `resources` glob in any of the six tauri config variants covers that path — every glob is rooted at src-tauri/SIDECAR/, a different directory. What ships is generated: bin/stage-env-sidecars.sh does `rm -rf $SIDECAR/env-sidecars` then `cp -al $SIDECAR/spa $ENV_SC/spa`, hardlink-copying the PRIMARY sidecar SPA, which does not contain these pages. bin/build-windows-cross.sh independently rm -rf's and re-stages the top-level dir before building.

Root cause of the residue: that directory is a committed BUILD ARTIFACT the build regenerates. Independently corroborated by EI-20555742146560765, which measured 4,483 tracked files under the same path and 2,418 self-dirtied entries during the 0.0.17 release cut. The two pages were stale content dating to 2026-07-07, from when the primary SPA still had them.

My own instrument error, recorded so it does not recur: the initial `git ls-files | grep el-` was run from the SUPERPROJECT and returned nothing, which made tracked files look like untracked stray output. git ls-files does not recurse into submodules and papercusp-desktop is one.

checked: el-bare-test.html removed from the tracked artifact
el-fresh-test.html removed from the tracked artifact
residue: The not-shipped claim rests on packaging config + generator scripts + absence from built output on this box. No published installer exists here to crack open; confirming absence inside one would close the last gap.
Tracking of the 4,483-file regenerated build artifact remains open (see deferred).
population: el-bare-test.html removed from the tracked artifact
el-fresh-test.html removed from the tracked artifact

deferred: The underlying defect is NOT fixed and was deliberately not taken: a 4,483-file regenerated build artifact is tracked at all, which EI-20555742146560765 measured defeating the gitDirty==false release ship-gate on every successful cut. Untracking it is a cross-lane change touching the release provenance gate and is not mine to make unilaterally from a voice-release lane. Recorded on the item for whoever owns that gate.
terminalCompletionEvidence.testsRun: No test suite applies — this removed two unreferenced static HTML files from a regenerated build artifact. Verification was direct inspection of the packaging path.
terminalCompletionEvidence.coordNotes:
git ls-files from a superproject silently omits submodule contents, so an empty grep reads as 'untracked stray file' when the file is tracked
This produced a wrong severity assessment that survived into a filed work-item title ('still ships') and would have shipped as a release-blocker claim. The tell is that an absence was proved by a single command in a single tree; the repo has submodules, so absence needs the submodule-aware form. Same class as the playbook's 'an absence proved by one grep in one file' rule, one level up: here the instrument's SCOPE, not the file, was the blind spot.
terminalCompletionEvidence.testResult: passed: both files absent after removal; `git status --porcelain` in the submodule shows ' D' for each; `stat` showed link count 1 on each before deletion (no shared inode with the primary SPA, so nothing else was affected); primary SPA src-tauri/sidecar/spa/ untouched and never contained them; no ElevenLabs HTML page remains under the staging SPA; nothing in the repo references either page by name.
